text: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel,

they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the families and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to him ever since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of Israel's families answered them, "You have nothing to do with us in building a house for our God. We ourselves will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, just as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us."
Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah and making them afraid to build.

versions.text: Then the people of the land set out to weaken the hands of the people of Judah and to make them afraid to build.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses participles (מְרַפִּים ... וּמְבַהֲלִים) describing continuous action that actually took place, not merely an intention. "Set out to" introduces the idea of purpose that is not in the text; the participial rendering also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: They bribed officials to work against them and frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and on into the reign of Darius king of Persia.
In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic script and set out in the Aramaic language.
Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows:

From Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is, the Elamites,
together with the rest of the peoples whom the great and honorable Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and elsewhere in the province Beyond the River. And now:
This is a copy of the letter they sent him: To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men of the province Beyond the River. And now:

Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have arrived at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city; they are finishing its walls and repairing its foundations.
Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will pay no tribute, tax, or toll, and the royal revenue will suffer.
Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not right for us to watch the king be dishonored, we send this word to inform the king,

so that a search may be made in the record books of your fathers. In those records you will find and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that from ancient times revolt has been stirred up within it. That is why this city was laid waste.
We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will no longer have any holding in the province Beyond the River.

The king sent this reply: To Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River: Greetings. And now:
The letter you sent us has been read out clearly in my presence.
I gave the order, and a search was made, and it was found that this city has risen against kings from ancient times, and that rebellion and revolt have been carried on in it.
Mighty kings have ruled in Jerusalem and governed the whole province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
Now give the order to make these men stop, so that this city is not rebuilt until I issue a further decree.
See that you are not negligent in this matter. Why should the damage grow and the kings be harmed?
As soon as the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they hurried to the Jews in Jerusalem and forced them to stop by force of arms.

versions.text: As soon as the copy of King Artaxerxes' letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they hurried to the Jews in Jerusalem and forced them to stop by strength of arms.
versions.explanation: "Artaxerxes' letter" is awkward for oral reading (a possessive on a name ending in -es); the of-phrase reads more naturally. "By force of arms" is the more idiomatic English rendering of בְּאֶדְרָע וְחָיִל.

text: So the work on the house of God in Jerusalem came to a halt, and it stood still until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
